headline: Remains of 12 slaughtered horses found in Gazipur forest
summary: Authorities recovered heads, hides, and bones in Sreepur, suspecting the animals were killed for their meat.
details: The remains of at least 12 horses were discovered in a forest in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur early Monday morning.
The remains, including heads, hides, legs, intestines, and bones, were found in the Mudipara area, near the Karnapur-Barmi regional road.
Local residents first spotted the body parts scattered along a narrow footpath leading into the forest while they were collecting grass.
Sreepur Upazila Livestock Officer Ashraf Hossain confirmed that the horses were slaughtered and their meat had been taken away.
Police and law enforcement agencies visited the scene to investigate the incident and identify those responsible.
Authorities have stated that legal action will be taken against the perpetrators once they are identified.
Arrangements are being made to bury the remains recovered from the forest.
caption:
12 horses slaughtered and dumped in a forest. Their meat was taken, leaving only the remains behind.

The remains of at least 12 horses were discovered in a forest in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur early Monday morning.

The remains, including heads, hides, legs, intestines, and bones, were found in the Mudipara area, near the Karnapur-Barmi regional road.

Local residents first spotted the body parts scattered along a narrow footpath leading into the forest while they were collecting grass.

Sreepur Upazila Livestock Officer Ashraf Hossain confirmed that the horses were slaughtered and their meat had been taken away.

Police and law enforcement agencies visited the scene to investigate the incident and identify those responsible.

Authorities have stated that legal action will be taken against the perpetrators once they are identified.

Arrangements are being made to bury the remains recovered from the forest.

headline_marked: UN report on Al-Qaeda in Bangladesh [[is speculative]], says Home Minister
headline: UN report on Al-Qaeda in Bangladesh is speculative, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed dismissed a UN Security Council report regarding the expansion of Al-Qaeda in the Indian subcontinent within Bangladesh.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that a UN report on the expansion of Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) in Bangladesh is based on speculation and is not being acted upon by the current government.
Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat on Monday, the Minister noted that while he had heard of the report, he had not yet read it in full, though it may contain some observations.
The UN Security Council had previously expressed concern that Al-Qaeda was attempting to use Bangladesh to establish terrorist cells in the Indian subcontinent.
Regarding domestic security, the Home Minister claimed that the law and order situation has improved, although he admitted that more time is needed to meet public expectations.
He also addressed the energy crisis, stating that fuel and gas shortages were legacy issues from the previous 'fascist' government that cannot be resolved overnight.
To reduce reliance on imports, the government has initiated new gas exploration efforts on land and in the sea, hoping to solve the crisis within a few years.
caption:
The Home Minister has dismissed a UN report on Al-Qaeda's expansion in Bangladesh as 'speculative'.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that a UN report on the expansion of Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) in Bangladesh is based on speculation and is not being acted upon by the current government.

Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat on Monday, the Minister noted that while he had heard of the report, he had not yet read it in full, though it may contain some observations.

The UN Security Council had previously expressed concern that Al-Qaeda was attempting to use Bangladesh to establish terrorist cells in the Indian subcontinent.

Regarding domestic security, the Home Minister claimed that the law and order situation has improved, although he admitted that more time is needed to meet public expectations.

He also addressed the energy crisis, stating that fuel and gas shortages were legacy issues from the previous 'fascist' government that cannot be resolved overnight.

To reduce reliance on imports, the government has initiated new gas exploration efforts on land and in the sea, hoping to solve the crisis within a few years.

#Bangladesh #Security #UN #AlQaeda #Politics #Dhaka

Source: Jamuna TV
